summary: Diego Cosmelli earned his PhD at the École Polytechnique, studying under doctoral supervisor Francisco Varela.

Diego Loukota works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an MA from Peking University and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, in 2019.

Dieter B. Kapp (1941–2021) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at Heidelberg University under Hermann Berger, later holding posts there, including außerplanmäßiger Professor (1987), and serving as Director of Indology and Tamilistics at Cologne (1990–2006).
Dieter Conrad (1932–2001) worked in Indology and other fields. He earned his Dr.iur. at Heidelberg University (circa 1957–1963) and served there as a Senior Research Fellow from 1963 to 1997.

Dieter George (1935–1985) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau, worked at the Royal Library of Berlin (circa 1969–1985), and served as Geschäftsführer of the DMG (1977–1985).

Dieter Gunkel (born 1981) is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Middlebury College and UCLA (PhD 2010). He held posts at the University of Munich (2010–2017) and University of Richmond (2017–2024) before joining UCLA in 2024.

Dieter Schlingloff (born 1928) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen. He held posts at the GDR Academy of Sciences, Kiel University (1968–1971), and the University of Munich (1972–1996).
Dieter Schrapel is an Indologist who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg under the supervision of Wilhelm Rau (attested 1970).

Dieter Schuh (born 1942) is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD and habilitation at the University of Bonn. He served as professor of Tibetology at Bonn (1978–2007) and founded the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Diether Lauenstein (1914–1990) specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tübingen and earned a Dr.theol. at Marburg under Johannes Nobel, later completing his habilitation and holding a post at the University of Greifswald in 1944.

Dietmar Rothermund (1933–2020) was a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. He had a long career at Heidelberg University, serving as Chair of the History of South Asia from 1968 to 2001.
Dieuke Gaastra was an Indology scholar who studied at Utrecht University under Willem Caland and Johan Hendrik Gallée, completing a PhD in 1906.

Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (1910–1991) was a prominent figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Shechen Gyaltsap and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, succeeding Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje from 1987 to 1991.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti (born 1941) is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta. He taught archaeology at Calcutta (1965–1977), the University of Delhi (1977–1990), and the University of Cambridge (1990–2008).

Dilip Kumar Biswas (1920–2003) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, later holding posts at Visva-Bharati University and the University of Calcutta.

Dilli Raman Regmi (1914–2001) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Madras and earned a D.Litt. from Patna University (1961), later teaching at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Dina Bangdel (1964–2017) specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held academic posts at Ohio State University (circa 2002–2007) and Virginia Commonwealth University (circa 2007–2017).

Dina Johanna Kohlbrugge (1911–1999) was an Indology and Iranian studies scholar. She earned her PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and served there as Professor of Modern Persian and Iranian language and literature (1949–1981).

Dines Andersen (1861–1940) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Copenhagen under Fausbøll, Thomsen, and Verner. He spent his career at Copenhagen as a librarian, docent, and professor (1903–1927).

Dineschandra Sircar (1907–1985) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and later held the Carmichael Professorship at the University of Calcutta starting in 1962.
